clerk.text: Awright? Today's runners are up on the screens. Pick yer beast, write yer line, and nae arguing wi' the screen, it never listens.

then.text: Keep the limit and keep your head. And keep that number somewhere you'll find it.

else.text: Forty years of Saturdays, son. I'll tell you what the board never shows. What it costs.

Bookies shade every price so the house wins over time. And down at the casino, the roulette wheel has 37 pockets but pays as if there were 36. That green zero is the house's cut: about 2.7p in every pound, for good.
Which of these is a warning sign?
options: Setting a limit before you go in
Chasing your losses to win it back
Leaving when you hit the limit

then.text: Not that one. That's the sensible one. Keep going.
Aye. That's the big one. The next bet that 'puts it right' is how a bad night becomes a bad year.
That's the good habit, not the warning sign. Well done for hearing it though.

else.text: Other signs: hiding it, borrowing to play, spending more than you meant, or it stopping being fun. Treat what you bring as the price of a night out and not an investment.

If it's getting on top of you, or someone you love, in Great Britain the National Gambling Helpline is 0808 8020 133. Free, confidential, all hours, and no judgement. For online sites, there's a free scheme called GAMSTOP that blocks you from them.
Saying it out loud is the hard bit. It gets a lot easier after that. Here, have a wee pudding. My wife made it.
Noted in the Almanac under Things worth knowing.
